rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 6 compounds and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. This should reveal whether early peaks are unretained, whether late peaks need strong solvent, and where the critical adjacent resolutions lie.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to shorten the run. Keeping the same wide window and temperature while reducing tG tests how much compression is possible before any pair drops below baseline resolution.

CRF is already at the maximum, so now the goal is to find the shortest robust fully resolved method. Decreasing tG one step while holding phi-window and temperature fixed probes how much more time can be cut before the first adjacent pair starts to approach the 1.5 threshold.

Resolution is still comfortably above the 1.5 threshold for all pairs, with the limiting pair now (1,2), so the next logical move is to shorten the gradient again. This will define how far run time can be reduced before the earliest pair becomes critical.

The method remains far from the resolution limit even at tG 8 min, so shortening to 6 min is the most efficient way to locate the onset of failure. The earliest pair continues to be the likely limiter, and this step should still retain a comfortable margin if the system is broadly forgiving.

At tG 6 min the limiting pair is still well above R = 1.5, so another reduction in gradient time is warranted to approach the true minimum-time fully resolved method. This should reveal whether the first two peaks are near the practical compression limit or whether additional time savings remain.

The critical pair is now just above the 1.5 cutoff at tG 4 min, so testing the minimum allowed gradient time will determine whether this is already the optimum or whether the method can be shortened one more step. This directly brackets the resolution limit for the fastest possible fully resolved run.

We have bracketed the fastest full-resolution point in tG, so now optimize robustness by easing the overly broad low-organic start. Raising phi0 should shorten the run further while checking whether the critical early pair remains above R = 1.5 or starts to collapse.

The first pair improved slightly when phi0 was raised to 0.10, indicating the very early region can be trimmed without harming selectivity. A further increase in phi0 should test whether the gradient window can be tightened to make the 4 min method more efficient while keeping the critical pair above threshold.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.15 consistently improved the limiting early-pair resolution while keeping all compounds within a very short run, so one more step should locate the best trimmed start. This probes whether the first peaks are still spending too much time in unnecessarily weak solvent.

The 4 min runs show phi0 around 0.15–0.20 gives the best margin on the limiting first pair, so now test whether that improved starting composition can rescue the 2 min gradient. If it succeeds, it would define a faster fully resolved method than the current 4 min optimum.

The limiting pair is controlled, and all compounds elute well before the end of the gradient, so the high-end window is probably broader than needed. Lowering phi1 one step while keeping the successful 4 min, phi0 0.15 method should test whether the gradient can be tightened further without sacrificing full resolution.

Reducing phi1 to 0.90 improved the critical first-pair resolution, suggesting the gradient window is still wider than necessary at the high end. One more step down in phi1 should further tighten the useful elution window while keeping all peaks inside the gradient and fully resolved.

Narrowing the gradient window to phi1 0.85 has materially improved the limiting pair, so the next key test is whether this tighter window can make the 2 min gradient fully resolved. If successful, it would beat the current fastest robust 4 min method while preserving complete separation.

The tighter high-end window continues to improve the critical first pair, so pushing phi1 down one more step at tG 4 min should test the narrowest practical gradient that still cleanly elutes all compounds. This may provide enough additional selectivity to support a later retry at the 2 min limit.

At tG 4 min, lowering phi1 to 0.80 has given the strongest margin yet on the limiting first pair, so this is the best candidate to revisit the 2 min gradient. This test will show whether the narrowed window is now sufficient to cross the R = 1.5 threshold at the minimum gradient time.

The limiting pair continues to improve as phi1 is lowered, and the last peak still elutes comfortably, so another step down in phi1 is justified at the proven 4 min condition. This should identify whether further narrowing of the gradient window can maximize selectivity for the critical early pair before risking excessive retention of the last compound.

The 4 min method at phi1 0.75 gives the best margin yet for the limiting pair, so this is the strongest remaining candidate for a successful 2 min full-resolution run. Testing it now determines whether continued window narrowing can finally lift the first pair above R = 1.5 at the minimum gradient time.

The 2 min runs improve steadily as phi1 is lowered, and the last peak remains comfortably early, so the most informative next step is to continue narrowing the high-end window at the minimum gradient time. This directly tests whether the limiting first pair can finally reach full credit at tG 2 min.

The 2 min method is converging on full resolution as phi1 decreases, and all six compounds still elute quickly, so one more reduction in phi1 is the highest-value experiment. This should show whether the limiting first pair can cross R = 1.5 while staying within an acceptably short run.

The limiting pair is now just below full-credit resolution at phi1 0.65, so one final decrease in phi1 is the most direct way to test whether a 2 min gradient can reach CRF 1.000. The last peak is still early enough that this extra retention should remain acceptable if all six compounds stay observed.

Now that a 2 min gradient has achieved full resolution, the remaining opportunity is to trim unnecessary low-organic hold and shorten the run further while keeping the first pair above R = 1.5. Raising phi0 one step at the successful phi1 0.60 condition is the cleanest way to test for a faster equally perfect method.

Raising phi0 to 0.20 preserved full resolution and slightly improved the limiting pair, so one more step tests whether the start can be trimmed further without pushing the first peak into the near-unretained region. This is the best remaining route to a still faster robust 2 min method.

At phi0 0.25 the first peak is still retained and the critical pair remains above threshold, so one more increase in phi0 can probe the practical upper limit of start strength for the fastest 2 min method. This checks whether a slightly more aggressive start further trims early retention or begins to erode the limiting separation.

The best 2 min full-resolution region is around phi0 0.20–0.25 and phi1 0.60, while lowering phi1 consistently improved the limiting pair until full resolution was reached. With the last injection, tighten the high end one more step from the successful phi0 0.20, phi1 0.60 condition to test for a still stronger margin on the critical pair without sacrificing full elution.
